name: Adhesives, Sealants & Construction Chemicals
tagline: The invisible products that decide whether the visible ones last
description: Nobody photographs the tile adhesive, and nobody forgets it when the tiles come loose. This section covers the wet trades' chemistry — bonding, sealing, waterproofing and filling — with the substrate and cure requirements that make each one work.

materials.name: Wood adhesive
materials.blurb: PVA white glue — the carpenter's everyday bond
materials.description: Water-based PVA for timber-to-timber joints, applied thinly to both faces and clamped. Choose a water-resistant grade for anything near a kitchen or bathroom.

materials.name: Laminate adhesive
materials.blurb: Contact cement for bonding laminate to board
materials.description: Applied to both surfaces, left to tack off and then pressed — there is no repositioning once the two faces meet. Ventilation matters: solvent grades are strong and flammable.

materials.name: Epoxy adhesive
materials.blurb: Two-part structural bond for stone, metal and repairs
materials.description: Mixed resin and hardener that cures to a rigid, gap-filling bond stronger than most substrates. Used for stone repairs, anchoring bolts and joining dissimilar materials.

materials.name: Silicone sealant
materials.blurb: Flexible weatherproof seal for glass, sanitary and joints
materials.description: Neutral-cure for stone and metal, acetoxy for glass and ceramic, anti-fungal for wet areas. The wrong cure type will stain marble or fail to stick — read the label, not the colour.

materials.name: PU adhesive / sealant
materials.blurb: Polyurethane bond that stays flexible and paints over
materials.description: Tougher and more elastic than silicone, and unlike silicone it can be painted. The right choice for structural joints, façade seals and bonding panels that will move.

materials.name: Tile adhesive
materials.blurb: Cement-based adhesive, graded by tile type and position
materials.description: The days of sand-cement dabs are over — large-format vitrified tiles need a graded adhesive with full-bed coverage. Match the grade to the tile size, substrate and whether it is a wall or a pool.

materials.name: Tile grout
materials.blurb: Cement or epoxy joint filler — epoxy where stains matter
materials.description: Cement grout is cheap and absorbs everything; epoxy grout resists stains and chemicals completely and is what a kitchen backsplash or a bathroom floor deserves.

materials.name: Waterproofing membrane
materials.blurb: Liquid or sheet barrier under every wet floor
materials.description: Applied before tiling in bathrooms, balconies and terraces, turned up the wall and tested by ponding for 24–48 hours. The one item where cutting cost guarantees a callback.

specs.Type: Cementitious / acrylic / PU liquid, or sheet

materials.name: Wood filler
materials.blurb: Putty that fills nail holes and grain before finishing
materials.description: Shade-matched filler pressed into holes and open grain, sanded flush before polishing. Choose the shade against the finished sample, not the raw timber — it darkens under polish.

materials.name: Wall putty
materials.blurb: White cement or acrylic skim that levels plaster
materials.description: Two coats sanded flat give paint a surface worth applying to. Acrylic putty is more flexible and better for interiors; white cement putty is cheaper and works on exteriors.

materials.name: Construction sealant (acrylic)
materials.blurb: Paintable gap filler for internal joints and cracks
materials.description: Fills the junction between skirting and wall, architrave and plaster, and hairline cracks — then takes paint straight over. Not for wet areas or moving structural joints.
